rows: 2022 Annual General Meeting (Annual Meeting of Shareholders)
Meeting held remotely because CEO John Fieldly tested positive for COVID; 2021 framed as a 'monumental' and 'foundational' year.
2022 framed as 'the year of optimization and execution' with the national DSD network (288 distributors, ~98% population coverage) as a key strategic asset.
DSD network improves in-store execution, SKU count, dry-shelf-to-display placement, and cold placements; enables servicing of smaller regional chains, raising ACV.
Q1 revenue growth was largely volume-driven, not pricing-driven; North American growth came from triple-digit traditional-channel growth plus SKU/cold-placement/end-cap optimization.
Gross margin decline (40.4% vs 41.1%) attributed to higher raw material costs, customer mix and supply chain inflation; higher-cost imported international cans flow through COGS to end of Q3.
Channel incrementality: expansion in historically underrepresented convenience and club channels has not impacted growth in other channels.
Club channel (Costco nationwide, Sam's Club initial orders, BJ's testing) expected to be a material part of the business in 2022 and beyond.
Convenience described as 'the biggest opportunity we see ahead' (70% of energy sold there).
Innovation pipeline: Strawberry Lemonade summer flavor, successful 7-Eleven Mango Passionfruit launch, Arctic Vibe extension penetrating traditional convenience.
Adjacent portfolio (Celsius Heat, BCAA) to follow once core lines are solidified; core line has 15+ flavors.
International approached deliberately and profitably: active distributor discussions across UK/Germany (via Amazon) and Asia (Australia, South Korea, Japan); North America remains primary focus.
Health-and-wellness is a global megatrend; post-pandemic recovery of fitness and vending channels (especially micro-markets) noted as a tailwind.
European supply chain disruption cited as a factor in the ~10% Q1 international revenue decline.
NOTE: CEO's section cited Q1 net income of $66.2M, conflicting with CFO's $6.7M; $6.7M is the reliable figure (transcription error).
International initiatives over the next 12 months
What are the real interests for international initiatives over the next 12 months?

Sees great opportunity in Asia and Europe but takes a deliberate, incremental, profitable-growth approach; cited Finland/Norway and UK/Germany via Amazon, plus Asian activity (Australia fitness distributor, South Korea partner, Japan); timing/sequencing/cost-structure matter; North America remains the primary focus.
All Board nominees elected; Ernst & Young LLP ratified as auditor for FY2022; advisory say-on-pay vote approved. Meeting adjourned by the Corporate Secretary.
